package_info.package_manager: N/A (Injected JavaScript in e-commerce site HTML)
package_info.package_versions: N/A (Script block in live site HTML)
package_info.why_malicious: The script is a digital skimmer that exfiltrates sensitive customer data, specifically address and credit card information, from the checkout page to a remote attacker-controlled server. This results in theft of payment data, a severe breach of user privacy, and undermines the integrity of the e-commerce platform.

execution_context.trigger: At runtime, when the user loads and interacts with the checkout page
execution_context.file_location: Inline <script> block embedded in the checkout page HTML

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, when the user interacts with the checkout page, the code accesses the credit card and address input fields from the DOM, serializes this sensitive data, and sends it via HTTP POST to a hardcoded attacker-controlled domain, resulting in exfiltration of payment and personal information.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code programmatically collects sensitive user input (credit card and address) from the checkout form and transmits it to an external domain ('https://attacker-server.com/collect') that is not affiliated with the legitimate e-commerce site. The use of obfuscation further indicates an attempt to evade detection.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate checkout page scripts should only transmit payment data to trusted payment processors or internal endpoints, never to unknown or untrusted third-party servers. They should also avoid obfuscation unless justified and reviewed.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate analytics or payment processing scripts may collect form data, but only send it to vetted, trusted endpoints (such as PCI-compliant payment gateways) and typically with user consent and visible privacy disclosures.
key_indicators: Direct access to sensitive form fields (e.g., input[name="credit_card"], input[name="address"])
Outbound HTTP POST request to an untrusted, hardcoded external domain
Presence of obfuscated or minified inline JavaScript in critical checkout page templates
No user notification or consent for data transmission

attack_chain.action: A malicious script is injected into the checkout page HTML, either by compromising the site or via a third-party dependency.
attack_chain.leads_to: The skimmer code is loaded and ready to execute in the user's browser.

attack_chain.action: As the user enters payment and address information, the script executes in the browser, harvesting sensitive form data from the DOM.
attack_chain.leads_to: Sensitive data is collected and prepared for exfiltration.

attack_chain.action: The collected credit card and address data is serialized and sent via HTTP POST to the attacker's remote server.
attack_chain.leads_to: The attacker receives stolen payment and address information, enabling fraud or resale.

behavioral_signatures: JavaScript accessing payment or address form fields (e.g., input[name="credit_card"], input[name="address"]) on checkout pages
Outbound HTTP POST requests from checkout pages to domains not associated with the e-commerce site or its payment providers
Presence of obfuscated or minified inline scripts within sensitive page templates (e.g., checkout.html)
file_indicators: Unexpected <script> blocks embedded directly in checkout or payment page HTML
References to external JavaScript files loaded from untrusted or previously unseen domains in checkout page source
network_indicators: HTTP POST requests from user browsers on checkout pages to unknown or suspicious domains (e.g., 'attacker-server.com')
Unusual outbound traffic patterns from checkout pages, especially containing serialized payment or address data
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Continuously monitor the source code of checkout and payment pages for unauthorized or obfuscated script blocks. Use web application firewalls (WAF) or browser instrumentation to detect JavaScript accessing sensitive form fields and making outbound requests to domains not on an allowlist of trusted payment or analytics providers. Correlate network logs for POST requests containing payment or address data sent to external domains, and alert on any such activity to domains not explicitly approved.
